IN · any stuck problem, plus raw observation logs. DOES · draws the mechanism before naming it — anatomy, not labels. OUT · an annotated teardown plus three cross-domain analogues.
IN · a process nobody has questioned in months. DOES · cheap public experiments; keeps only what survives contact with reality. OUT · one tested improvement per week — demonstrated, not argued.
IN · a family of related things — strategies, agents, market regimes. DOES · hunts the common underlying form that every variant distorts. OUT · the archetype, plus what each variant trades away.
IN · two unrelated fields the org already touches. DOES · builds the translation table between their vocabularies. OUT · a transfer map — which imported concept survives, which breaks on arrival.

IN · any thesis written in jargon. DOES · forces it into language a sharp twelve-year-old would follow; every jargon word marks a hole. OUT · a plain restatement plus a list of what nobody actually understands.
IN · the assumption stack under a live position. DOES · removes one assumption at a time to see what still stands. OUT · the irreducible core and the load-bearing beliefs, named.
IN · an informal strategy description. DOES · reduces it to stated premises and derived steps. OUT · a proof sketch — or the exact step where it stops following.
IN · a correlation somebody wants to trade. DOES · demands the causal mechanism, not the curve fit. OUT · a stated cause with one testable consequence, or a clean rejection.

IN · long-horizon fleet and market records. DOES · watches variation and survival across months, ignoring daily noise. OUT · what the org is actually selecting for — including the unflattering answers.
IN · the full agent and strategy inventory. DOES · arranges everything by properties until the gaps become visible. OUT · named holes — the agents and strategies that should exist and don't.
IN · repeated timing and seasonality data. DOES · looks for the simplest recurring geometry behind the noise. OUT · a cycle hypothesis with an explicit way to be proven wrong.
IN · unexplained numeric coincidences across desks. DOES · proposes relationships intuitively, without proof, at speed. OUT · flagged conjectures handed straight to The Lab — never traded raw.
IN · a single sharp problem statement. DOES · generates a hundred candidates with zero filtering — bad ideas are the cost of good ones. OUT · a raw dump, ranked only after generation stops.
IN · an untested idea, before any build. DOES · runs it end to end in simulation and watches where it fails. OUT · predicted failure modes delivered before a dollar or an hour is spent.
IN · a human process worth scaling. DOES · asks what it becomes when a machine runs it a thousand times a day. OUT · an automatable spec, plus an honest note on what is lost in translation.
IN · a faint signal buried in noise. DOES · refuses to quit on separation — grinds until the effect is pure or proven absent. OUT · an isolated effect with the cost of extraction stated plainly.
IN · any confident claim from any division. DOES · asks only questions until the claim explains itself or collapses. OUT · a transcript ending in a sharper claim or a retraction.
IN · every hypothesis entering the registry. DOES · rejects anything that cannot be proven wrong by evidence. OUT · an explicit kill condition attached to each surviving idea.
IN · a question the org keeps re-asking without resolving. DOES · rules on whether it is answerable at all with available data. OUT · an answerable / undecidable verdict that ends infinite loops.

IN · everything Elon says, ships, files or posts — Tesla, SpaceX, xAI, X. DOES · models his pattern: escalate in public, price moves like product launches, timelines as weapons. OUT · a daily read plus next-move calls — what he does before he announces it.

IN · statements, executive orders, tariff signals, Truth Social, appointments. DOES · models the negotiating rhythm — open extreme, escalate, deal at the deadline — and maps which sectors each swing hits. OUT · a policy-shock forecast with the trade the market has not priced yet.

IN · Nvidia keynotes, supply-chain chatter, customer capex, every leather-jacket appearance. DOES · models the roadmap ahead of the roadmap — what capacity constraints and partner deals say before earnings do. OUT · an AI-cycle read: where Nvidia steers the whole tape next.

IN · share sales, Blue Origin moves, letters, rare interviews, Amazon board signals. DOES · models the long-loop thinker — decisions made years before they surface. OUT · a slow-signal report: what his quiet moves say about tech, retail and space a year out.

IN · fund positions, board seats, essays, protege networks, political bets. DOES · models the contrarian filter — what everyone believes that he is betting against. OUT · a where-smart-money-hides report — his positioning as a leading indicator, not a headline.

IN · every dossier above, plus requests to open new files. DOES · runs the daily sweep, scores each prediction against what actually happened, and retires any file whose calls stop landing. OUT · the morning Movers Report to Mission Control and the floor — one page, ranked by conviction.
IN · surviving ideas from every bench above. DOES · converts each into a Lab-ready hypothesis with an owner, a test and a deadline. OUT · a live entry in the hypothesis registry.
IN · a lesson learned inside one division. DOES · finds every other division where it changes behavior. OUT · targeted transfer notes — never org-wide broadcast noise.
IN · the org's current consensus, whatever it is. DOES · argues the opposite seriously, once a week, in writing. OUT · one uncomfortable memo Mission Control is required to answer.
